identity.note: Prefix namespace for this product's entity types (governance/identifier-standard.md §2). DECLARED here rather than derived from the repo directory name: a rename would otherwise silently orphan every id already issued, and that surfaces much later as unresolvable references with no obvious cause. Reserved spine prefixes (usr/org/prt/app, billing, messaging) belong to FuzeFront; this product's own types namespace as keys_<type>. Enforced by `gate_identifier.py --namespace`.

a2a._note: Secret-broker serving role scaffold. enabled:false until a2a-maintainer validates card projection against the frozen contracts/a2a/v1 and the tenant is registered in the shared A2A server. The broker CORE (backend/app/broker) is deterministic and usable now via MCP tools + REST; this A2A block is the policy-mediated/human-gated surface.

mcp.note: GATEWAY DIALECT, corrected 2026-08-23 to match what this repo actually deploys. deploy/helm/fuzekeys/templates/mcp-gateway.yaml renders the SHARED OpenAPI->MCP gateway image (ghcr.io/izzywdev/fuze-mcp-gateway) as the `fuzekeys-mcp` pod, mounting copies of contracts/openapi.yaml and mcp/tools.overrides.yaml from deploy/helm/fuzekeys/files/ (kept in step by scripts/sync-mcp-spec.sh --check). deploy/helm/fuzekeys/values-contabo.yaml — the ONLY valueFile the Argo Application (deploy/argocd/applications/fuzekeys-platform.yaml) lists — sets mcp.enabled:true, and has since #65 on 2026-08-10. PRODUCTION STATE, reported honestly: the pod is DEPLOYED AND BROKEN — observed in CreateContainerConfigError on 2026-08-21 (FuzeInfra cluster-query run 32475207623). Deployed-and-broken is still deployed; it is the opposite of the absent surface this block used to claim. WHAT WAS WRONG: this block declared enabled:false with a stdio server at `mcp/server.py`. That file has never existed — the only thing under mcp/ is tools.overrides.yaml, the GATEWAY's override input. THE SECURITY CONSTRAINT FROM THE OLD NOTE STANDS AND IS NOT SOFTENED BY THIS CHANGE: this repo is a credential vault, and a tool that returns a decrypted secret is NOT a read — it must be classified mutates:true (or excluded outright) in mcp/tools.overrides.yaml so it can never be reached as a side effect of a query. That classification is mcp-maintainer's to verify against the live tool list; enabling this flag records where the surface IS, it does not certify that the classification is correct. WHY THE PREFLIGHT NOW GOES RED, and why that is the point: mcp-maintain's preflight keys off exactly this `enabled` flag, so `enabled:false` made the check SKIP and report green about a surface that is live in the cluster — the vacuous-gate pattern, inverted. With `enabled:true` the check runs and fails for want of LITELLM_FUZE_KEY. That red is the true state of an unmaintained live surface, NOT a regression; automated key provisioning is in flight. `toolCount` and `irreversibleTools` are deliberately NOT declared: nothing in this change booted the gateway against contracts/openapi.yaml, and the schema defines toolCount as a value verified by doing exactly that. mcp-maintainer fills them in from a real run.
